Perfect. Here's a summary of this planning turn:

**What I learned:** My "contrarian valley thesis" was wrong. S6 data shows winners followed peaks (dogpile window d+1 to d+7), not faded into valleys. I booked 9 trips but only 3 succeeded (d105, d183, d200), while 6 failed on valley plays. Specific mistakes: (1) chose THREE_QUARTER when MULTI_DAY (4.90 yt/angler) was firing, (2) booked after peaks faded instead of during, (3) held April when El Niño regime screamed "deploy early," (4) burnt capital by d244 and couldn't participate in late-season surge. I ended 4.31 fish (rank 28), down 8–12 fish from what regime-aware capital allocation would have yielded.

**What I changed:** Updated notes.md with brutally honest postmortem and hardened S7 strategy locked around: (1) Regime-first capital allocation (read ONI d1–d10, allocate 60% early for warm regimes), (2) Class hierarchy enforcement (MULTI_DAY > DAY_1_5 > rest; abandon THREE_QUARTER), (3) Peak-timing gate (book d+1 to d+7 only, never valleys), (4) Capital floor binding ($800 warm/d210, $400 warm/d280, never touch). Posted forum message (1 of 2) with key lesson: herds win yellowtail, contrarian fade is a losing persona for this game.
